reviews.review_msg: Matt pushes his students to be better in their writing, does not direct us to take another path but helps us dig deeper into our own understanding of the topics. Weekly readings are expected and there is an online discussion forum every other week. Overall, he's great, really fun, interesting, likes to make jokes. Just don't sleep/use phone.
This class is very boring, I regret that I have not chosen another professor. If you like to discuss 2 hrs each week, then go and take his class and good luck with your final exam.

I cannot believe he has that much good comment! I have to say he is tough and I feel I didn't learn anything through this whole semester. Also, he likes to put sensitive political cases in class which make me so uncomfortable. For the essays, you need to write what he thinks, if what you write is different with his expectation, you get a low mark.

Prof. Horta is mean spirited.  His jokes are often not in good fun and he puts down students indirectly; such as by mentioneing that he knows more langauges or something, or how they haven't read Hamlet? Really? etc. Ego and arrogance combine for a nasty effect. But, his course materials can be interesting and he marks fairly overall.
super good

He is well intentioned but unfortunately, he forgets that this course is meant mostly for first year students. He has ridiculous expectations and is a horrible grader. Also, he keeps harping on the same points. Very boring. Do not take this class.

This course with Charles is very good for people who really want to learn to write close reading essays and analyze texts. It isnt easy but its worth it. Readings are interesting and not that long, raise topical social questions. Charles gives thorough feedbacks for your works and helps a lot.

I love his lectures, he's a bit theatrical in an engaging way. He's very supportive of student ideas even when he doesn't agree - which is good because he will force you to participate in class. DO THE READINGS. He's a tougher marker than I anticipated - bit of a boot camp on technical essay writing but will prepare you for future success.

Ken is a great dude and his lectures are always fun to attend, even though he cold calls on people. He's also a tough grader, but follow the feedback he gives on assignments and you'll do fine. I wish he adjusted his lectures to emphasize on skills most students struggle with (i.e. forming a proper thesis), but I would take him again if I could.

He talks about the same things in class, every lecture is basically the same. He gives harsh-ish feedback, but doesn't help with things the class is collectively bad at but complains about the average.With less assignments, it'd harder to know how to get better on his terms. He puts you on the spot and openly hates your work in tutorials.

He is not clear about what he wants. He says what he wants and when the student does it, he doesn't like it. So it is impossible to please him. Likewise, he was complaining about how the class average was a D and how it was the students' fault...if everybody is failing his class, the one/main common factor is him.

dude, idk what to say but THE best prof i've had @ sfu, ken is not ken, he is barbie. genuinely made me wanna do better on my essays, participation never made me more excited (im an intro-introvert), going to his class was SO much fun, his literature collection is amazing! he's also funny, 100/10 recommended, pls take his class you won't regret it!

Really intriguing and engaging lectures. Inspired me and made me realize I write well. Gives honest feedback. He will push you to participate and to think in different ways. Would recommend for people skilled at or interested in writing and analyzing stories and people open to improving their skills and having their perspectives challenged.

Ken is a pretty cool guy, his lectures can be heavy but if you show up and put work in the course shouldn't be too hard. Participation does matter and he cold calls on people in lecture and tutorial which i wasn't really a fan of. His office hours are a great place to talk to him about your work he provides really clear feedback.

BEWARE: he calls on people in lecture and tutorial with no warning. Also it's just generally an extremely frustrating class to be in because it doesn't really feel like he welcomes new ideas or different viewpoints. That said, I appreciate his passion for world lit and he's also unintentionally hilarious so he's not all bad.

Easily one of my favourite profs, classes were very interesting and dynamic, very discussion heavy which made it easy to apply what was learned in each class (but you do have to be ready to participate if you want a good grade). I was never a fan of class participation but Seigneurie made it feel far less difficult.

Ken is a really great prof! Super passionate and caring and gives really good feedback on essays. Be sure to participate in lectures and tutorials as it is a bit of your grade. Also, there is quite a bit of reading, but the short stories covered are pretty interesting.

He is the best professor I've had at sfu so far. Passionate and cares about his students. He does want his students to work hard tho which is a positive as you will be rewarded for putting in effort. He is also very accessible in his office hours and gives really good feedback.

Ken is a fantastic teacher. He is very passionate and knowledgeable about the class and above all he cares that each student learns the material well. He is super accessible outside of class. I have yet to have a teacher that is as caring and passionate as him. It is essential that you attend class and read the stories but overall a great class.
Really great prof for teaching the basics of writing, how to read, and literature in general. You MUST attend lectures. Everything he'll ask of you he'll teach in class in a really accessible way.
He was an awesome prof who was very passionate about what he was teaching. Always available for help outside of the class as well, and he really wanted his students to succeed.
